evidence: The finding is upheld: the binder receipt records argv `--base HEAD~1 --print-candidate`, which computes a one-commit window, while the reviewed change spans seven commits from origin/dev. The receipt itself is not misleading -- its argv and cwd are part of the record, which is how the reviewer detected the scope -- but the disposition that referenced it presented it as evidence of binder acceptance of the landing tree, and it is not. That reference is what is corrected.

What that receipt actually attests, stated exactly: on a clean checkout at the recorded commit the gate answers rather than errors for a one-commit window, which is the shipped-checkout case its own suite covers. It is retained under that reading rather than deleted, because deleting it would move the very candidate this ledger binds.

Full-base binder result, recorded here rather than receipted, with the reason: `review_ledger_binding.py --repo-root . --base origin/dev` on the landing tree is the authoritative local check, and it cannot be receipt-bound at all. A gate receipt carries `candidate_commit`, not a top-level `candidate_sha256`, so the binder's own exclusion predicate treats it as bound content; committing a receipt of the full binder run would therefore change the candidate that receipt attests. That is a fixed point of the design, not an omission, and CI re-running the gate on the merge commit remains the deterministic authority.

Reproduction for a reviewer, one command at the landing tree: `python3 skills/skill-extraction-workflow/scripts/review_ledger_binding.py --repo-root . --base origin/dev`. Its verdict is recorded in this round's closeout log alongside the candidate digest the ledger binds.
